title: The Monthly Pack Lands in January. The Problem Started in November.
linkedin:
Most businesses run on a monthly financial rhythm. For eleven months of the year, that's more than enough.

Then Christmas trading hits, and for retailers, hospitality venues and trades finishing jobs before the shutdown, six weeks carry more financial weight than the rest of the year combined.

Here's the problem. The monthly management pack that would normally land in early January describes a month that's already over. The decision it should have informed, extend trading hours again, chase a debtor before everyone leaves for three weeks, hold the final stock order, has usually already passed by the time it arrives.

The pattern we see across owner-led businesses isn't that the numbers were wrong. It's that they arrived on the wrong clock.

This is part of why fractional CFO support is built in tiers rather than one fixed cadence. A steady business genuinely doesn't need weekly numbers. A business moving into a concentrated trading peak often gets far more value from stepping up to a weekly or fortnightly check-in for that window specifically, because the decisions sitting on top of the numbers need answers measured in days, not in the following month.

None of this means overhauling how the business runs for the rest of the year. It means recognising that the weeks carrying the most financial weight aren't always the weeks getting the most financial attention, and building a short, deliberate window where that changes before the peak starts rather than during it.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.

If your business is in the middle of Christmas trading right now, here's something worth checking: is your financial reporting keeping pace with how fast you're having to make decisions?

Most Queensland, New South Wales and Victorian SMEs run comfortably on a monthly reporting rhythm for most of the year. But the six or so weeks around Christmas often carry more financial weight than the rest of the year combined, extra rostering, stock committed weeks earlier landing as invoices, and debtors wanting extra time before everyone takes a break. A monthly pack that lands in January describes a month that's already finished, which means the decision it should have informed has usually already passed.

We're seeing more owner-led businesses step up to a tighter, weekly or fortnightly check-in just for this trading peak, then step back to their usual monthly rhythm once January settles down. It's a small, temporary change that matches the pace of reporting to the pace of the decisions actually being made.

If you're trading flat out right now and haven't looked closely at the numbers since the peak started, it's worth a look. Read the full piece on the blog.
